items.title: Oracle：已确保履行与 OpenAI 合同全部所需资金
items.description: IT之家 11 月 22 日消息，Oracle（甲骨文）当地时间本月 20 日表示， 该企业已在本月初筹集到了履行与 OpenAI 交易的全部所需租金 ，与供应商进行的任何进一步私下讨论仅为补充选项。 ▲ Abilene Oracle 称其与 OpenAI 在 AI 基础设施合作方面的进展迅速： 位于美国得克萨斯州 Abilene 的园区已用于 GPT-6 Astra 的训练 ， 整体接近完工 ；下一个 GW 级项目 Shackelford 已获得所有许可；NVIDIA Vera Rubin 机架交付工作正按计划进行，预计将在未来几周内完成。 ▲ Shackelford 该企业仍预计可在 FY2028H2 实现正的自由现金流，目标是在 FY2029 实现超过 300 亿美元的自由现金流，并预计从届时起能够依靠自有资金支持未来增长。

items.content: 就在刚刚，Lean 和 Mathlib 社区发布联合声明，宣布正式认证 Anthropic 数学家 Levent Alpöge 提交的黎曼猜想形式化证明，并表示对其正确性具有充分信心。 更引人关注的是，Alpöge 此前透露，这项研究由他与 AI 模型 Claude 合作完成。在证明接近终点时，Claude 展现出的数学推理能力，甚至超出了他的预期。 11 月 20 日，Alpöge 在个人网站公布研究成果，宣称解决了著名的黎曼猜想（Riemann Hypothesis），同时取得了涉及广义黎曼猜想（Generalized Riemann Hypothesis）的结果。 它涉及黎曼 ζ 函数非平凡零点的分布，核心命题是所有非平凡零点的实部是否都等于 1/2。由于这一问题与素数分布密切相关，过去一个多世纪，无数数学家尝试攻克，却始终未能找到严格证明。 马斯克也发文感叹，证明黎曼猜想能够让大量此前依赖该猜想成立的数学结论摆脱条件限制，成为无条件成立的定理，并称其为超级智能取得的又一项惊人成就。 他曾尝试让 Claude 将证明整理成人类能够阅读的文字版本，结果生成的草稿超过 25 万页，庞大到连他本人都认为难以阅读。如此惊人的篇幅，甚至被部分网友戏称为一场针对数学界的「DDoS 攻击」。

items.content: 11 月 20 日，Anthropic 数学家 Levent Alpöge 在个人网站发布声明，称自己与 Claude 合作找到了黎曼猜想的证明，并表示同一方法还可以推广至广义黎曼猜想。目前，这一成果尚未经过独立验证。 黎曼猜想是数学界著名的「千禧年七大难题」之一，由德国数学家黎曼于 1859 年提出，涉及素数的分布规律。Alpöge 此次公开了一份 4 页说明，以及分成 14 个压缩包的 Lean 形式化证明文件，供其他研究者核查。 Alpöge 介绍，这项研究借鉴了数论中已有的证明思路，通过串联名为 theta 提升的数学变换，模拟传统方法中的「重数」作用。其中，Claude 提出让变换链的长度随求和范围的平方根增长，成为推进证明的关键思路之一。他表示，Claude 在研究后期的推进速度已经超过自己，接下来还将整理一份便于数学家理解的人类可读证明。 菲尔兹奖得主陶哲轩也于 11 月 20 日在个人博客提及此事。他指出，Alpöge 使用 AI 生成了一份规模庞大、仅以 Lean 代码呈现的广义黎曼猜想证明，理解和消化这份成果仍需要时间，但至少可以与人类作者沟通，协助完成这一过程。 目前，数学界仍需确认这些 Lean 文件能否独立通过校验，以及形式化定理是否准确对应黎曼猜想。陶哲轩的回应也不意味着证明已经获得认可。 三星电子 11 月 20 日宣布，由崔元俊接掌负责 Galaxy 手机的移动体验业务，卢泰文继续领导设备体验部门，并与负责半导体部门的全永铉共同担任 CEO。崔元俊自 2025 年 3 月起担任移动体验业务 COO，曾负责推动 Galaxy S26 和 Galaxy Z Fold8 系列上市。

items.content: 今天，知名半导体和 AI 研究机构 SemiAnalysis 在 X 上发了一张写给 Google DeepMind 主席 Demis Hassabis 的《向 Google 道歉专用表》。 理由一栏勾了包括「我只看了 X 上大家的消息」、「我那在 Anthropic 工作的室友，说服我相信 Gemini 已经完了」和「我没有阅读模型卡」等原因。最有意思的是最后一行：「Demis，关于 Gemini 4，我们错了。我们只想撤回一个词。」 他们从自己当初的标题里划掉了一个 is：Gemini is cooked。一句「Gemini 完了」，变成了「Gemini 这回真做出了点东西」。 事件的起因是 SemiAnalysis 在今年 8 月份发布了一篇文章，通篇都在讲 Google 自从去年 11 月短暂领先之后，就再也没有发布任何让人激动的模型，几乎是处在了掉队中的状态。 当时他们分析 DeepMind 的强化学习团队走了不少人，内部的算力又没分配好，对 Google 下了一个相当重的判断： 照这样下去，Google 当然还会继续发模型，但再一次达到行业最高水平的概率，已经「降到了零」。 报告发出不到两个月，谷歌就公布了 Gemini 4 Argon，接着 10 月底发布 Carbon、11 月 12 号推出 Hydrogen，18 号发布 Neon，短短 8 天的时间，接连推出了 3 款模型，其中 Carbon 的表现当时还来到了 Artificial Analysis 的综合能力榜首。

items.title: Signal restricts mobile screenshots as it confronts ‘existential threat’ of AI surveillance
items.description: Signal is limiting users' ability to take screenshots in both its Android and iOS apps.
items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: Signal announced Friday that it’s limiting users’ ability to take screenshots within the secure messaging app — a response to what President Meredith Whittaker described as the “existential threat” of operating systems that integrate agentic AI. Whittaker wrote that by giving AI agents the ability to “scan” the information on users’ screens, Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS “are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.” “Now, in service of AI agentic capabilities, your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” she said. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.” Signal already sought to limit these risks by blocking screenshots of its Windows app by default. Now it’s adding similar restrictions in Android and iOS. That said, users can disable this setting if they wish, which Whittaker said would “break our privacy guarantees.” She also admitted this is an “incomplete” solution, as it doesn’t “address other more sneaky ways AI agents could potentially access application data.” Get an Early Peek at the Next TechCrunch Disrupt Disrupt, Startup Battlefield, and more will return next year, and you can be at the front of the line. items.title: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages
items.description: We created a list of the most notable AI agents that can live in your text messages, from general assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.
items.author: Lauren Forristal
items.content: Rather than downloading another app, a growing number of agents can simply be texted like an ordinary person. You text it what you need, and it can remember context, connect to the apps and services you already use, and complete tasks on your behalf. That can mean scheduling an appointment, organizing a calendar, researching a trip, sending an email, making a reservation, shopping online, or reminding you about something days later. While Instinct is one of the buzziest AI agents at present, thanks to its $10 billion valuation after its latest funding round of $1 billion, there are many others also making a play for this space. Below are the most notable options so far, from general-purpose personal assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work. Ask Proxy ’s biggest differentiator is that it “thinks like a woman,” meaning it aims to anticipate your needs before you even ask, the company explains on its website. It works like a chatbot you can text like a friend, whether you need gift ideas, help planning an event, or recommendations for things to do that weekend. You can ask it to add important dates to your calendar, set reminders, or help with everyday decisions. You can also send it photos, like an empty table, to figure out how to decorate the table for a dinner party.

items.author: Lucas Ropek
items.content: For the most part, the content offered by the microdrama startup Shortical is indistinguishable from the rest of its industry . The company produces soapy, melodramatic storylines — almost always risqué romances — that, in bite-sized two-minute episodes, compel viewers to stay glued to their phones so as not to miss the latest twist in a tawdry, cliff-hanger-happy saga. The primary way that Shortical — which was founded last January — makes money is through subscriptions. Typically, the first 7-10 episodes of a micro-drama are free. After that, if the user wants to finish the series, they have to pay a small monthly fee which unlocks access to all of the site’s content. Over the past year, the company has churned out a gush of popular live-action romances like “Crossing the Line with My Neighbor,” “Accidentally Married My Boss,” and “Spoiled by My Billionaire Sugar Daddy.” Lately, however, the company’s homepage is covered in AI-generated content.
